plan.contextChunk: This figure contains two 2D vectors emanating from a common origin, illustrating the geometric definition of endpoint error in optical flow evaluation. The vector labeled (u, v) represents the ground truth flow vector, while the vector labeled (u-hat, v-hat) represents the predicted flow vector; both share the same base point but point in slightly different directions and have different magnitudes. A red line segment connects the tips (endpoints) of the two vectors, and this segment is labeled Endpoint error, making explicit that the loss is the Euclidean distance between the endpoint of the prediction and the endpoint of the ground truth. This figure establishes endpoint error as a vector-space distance metric, clarifying why it is sensitive to both directional and magnitude errors in the predicted flow field.

interactionPlan.concept: Endpoint error is the Euclidean (straight-line) distance between the tip of the predicted flow vector and the tip of the ground-truth flow vector, so it penalizes both directional and magnitude mistakes; angular error instead measures only the angle between the two vectors and is blind to magnitude.
elements: ground-truth flow vector (u,v): black arrow from origin pointing steeply up-right, with arrowhead and label '(u,v)' near its tip
predicted flow vector (û,v̂): black arrow from origin pointing right at a shallower angle, with arrowhead and label '(û,v̂)' near its tip
red line segment connecting the two vector tips, labeled 'Endpoint error'
angular-error arc at the origin spanning the angle between the two vectors, with an angle label θ (shown only in angular mode)
draggable handle markers at each vector tip

interactions.teaches: Endpoint error is exactly the tip-to-tip Euclidean distance: dragging the predicted tip (û,v̂) in any direction stretches or shrinks the red segment in real time, showing the loss grows with both a wrong direction and a wrong magnitude of the prediction
The ground-truth vector (u,v) fixes the reference endpoint; moving its tip repositions the red error segment, making clear that the error is always measured relative to wherever the true flow ends

interactions.label: Error metric
interactions.teaches: Switching to angular error replaces the tip-to-tip red segment with an arc at the origin measuring only the angle between the vectors — so scaling the prediction along its own direction changes endpoint error but leaves angular error unchanged, isolating the directional component of the mistake

demo_steps.title: Two flow vectors, one origin
demo_steps.narration: Both the ground-truth flow (u,v) and the predicted flow (û,v̂) start at the same pixel (the origin) but end at different points. The red segment joins their endpoints — that straight-line gap is the endpoint error.

demo_steps.title: Drag the prediction tip
demo_steps.narration: Drag (û,v̂): the red segment tracks the tip-to-tip distance live. Pull the prediction off in direction or shorten/lengthen it and the error grows — endpoint error conflates a directional mistake with a magnitude mistake.

demo_steps.title: Compare with angular error
demo_steps.narration: Toggle to angular error: the red tip segment is replaced by an arc at the origin measuring only the angle θ between the vectors. Now stretching the prediction along its own direction no longer changes the error — angular error sees direction but is blind to magnitude.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Endpoint error is a vector-space distance between predicted and true flow endpoints, so it is sensitive to both direction and magnitude; angular error removes the magnitude dependence by measuring only the angle between the two vectors.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Place the shared origin at the lower-left. Draw the ground-truth vector (u,v) steeply up-right (roughly 55–60° from horizontal) and the predicted vector (û,v̂) at a shallower angle (roughly 25–30°) and a bit shorter, both as solid black arrows with filled arrowheads. Label '(u,v)' just above-left of the ground-truth tip and '(û,v̂)' just below the predicted tip, in italic serif math style. Connect the two tips with a thick red segment and place the 'Endpoint error' label to its right. Add small circular drag handles at both tips. In angular-error mode, hide/dim the red tip segment and instead draw a colored (e.g. blue) arc at the origin between the two vector directions with a θ label, so the toggle visibly swaps a tip-distance cue for an origin-angle cue. Keep vectors black in both modes so only the error indicator changes.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Drag the estimated vector tip (û,v̂) in any direction and see the red endpoint error segment stretch or shrink in real time as the distance between the two vector tips updates
- Drag the ground-truth vector tip (u,v) to set a new reference flow direction and magnitude, watching the red error segment reposition accordingly
- Toggle between endpoint error (straight-line distance between vector tips) and angular error (angle between the two vectors) metrics, highlighting which geometric quantity each measures in the diagram

authoredInteractions:
- Drag the estimated vector tip (û,v̂) in any direction and see the red endpoint error segment stretch or shrink in real time as the distance between the two vector tips updates
- Drag the ground-truth vector tip (u,v) to set a new reference flow direction and magnitude, watching the red error segment reposition accordingly

authoredContext: In supervised optical flow estimation, the most common loss is the **endpoint error**, which is the average, over the whole image, if the distance between the estimated optical flow vector, $(\hat{u},\hat{v})$ and the ground-truth vector, $(u,v)$: $$\mathcal{L} \left( \hat{\mathbf{u}}, \hat{\mathbf{v}}, \mathbf{u}, \mathbf{v} \right) = \sum_{n,m} (\hat{u}[n,m] - u[n,m])^2 + (\hat{v}[n,m] - v[n,m])^2$$ The sum is over all the pixels in the image. Each pixel has an estimated optical flow $(\hat{u}[n,m],\hat{v}[n,m])$.

discrepancies: The predicted-vector label renders as '(û,v^)' — the circumflex on v appears as a detached caret/prime floating to the upper-right instead of a hat centered over the v, unlike the clean (û,v̂) in the source
White circular drag handles sit directly on the two arrowhead tips, partly covering the arrowheads and changing the clean tip look of the source
The drawing is compressed into the left ~60% of the canvas with a large right-hand control panel, so the overall composition is more cramped and left-shifted than the full-bleed source figure
evaluation.notes: Faithful, conceptually-correct interactive rendition: two black arrows from a shared origin, a red tip-to-tip 'Endpoint error' segment, plus genuinely useful drag-the-tip and endpoint/angular-metric-toggle interactions that correctly demonstrate the conflation of direction and magnitude; main flaws are the malformed v-hat glyph, the handle circles overlaying the arrowheads, and the left-compressed composition.
action_items: Fix the (û,v̂) label so the hat on v is centered over the letter (e.g. use a precomposed glyph, an SVG tspan with a manually drawn circumflex, or adjust the combining-character placement) instead of the current detached caret/prime
Make the drag handles smaller, semi-transparent, or visible only on hover so they do not obscure the black arrowhead tips that the source shows cleanly
Widen the SVG drawing region (or shrink/dock the control panel) so the two-arrow composition fills the frame more like the source rather than being squeezed into the left half

feedback.rationale: Overall average of 4.4 with all scores at 4-5, no failure modes, and only minor cosmetic issues (glyph rendering, handle size, layout spacing) that don't materially affect the figure's educational value or interactivity.
